A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same heatmap-guided MCTS study and GT-Prior approach despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hyperparameter-tuning experiments, GT-Prior evaluations, generalization tests, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations on nonuniform distributions and TSPLIB, including comparisons between tuning strategies.

M1.justification: The GT-Prior construction and MCTS initialization, k-opt search, selection, and weight updates remain unchanged. The published prior arrays and tuned configurations are identical. The newly emphasized tuning pipeline documents the existing grid-search procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained uniform TSP-500/1000/10000 experiments, v2 evaluates clustered, explosion, and implosion distributions and small, medium, and large Euclidean TSPLIB instances (Table 3 and Appendix F). This substantially expands the represented instance distributions and benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets are retained. Methods omitted from v2's shortened main benchmark table, including EAN, AM, GCN, POMO+EAS, and insertion heuristics, remain in Appendix C, Table 5. The added distribution and TSPLIB experiments use existing heatmap comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces evaluation protocols transferring uniform-derived heatmaps and tuned settings to nonuniform distributions. Its TSPLIB experiments compare default settings, uniform-tuned settings, and instance-level grid search, with results grouped by instance size. The original synthetic tuning-set sizes, search space, and stated time budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds distribution-shift robustness tests, TSPLIB tuning-transfer analysis, hard/easy instance case studies, and neighbor-prior statistics across distributions (Table 3, Appendix F, Figures 6–7). Figure 2 also expands tuning sensitivity reporting to configuration-performance distributions and extrema. The original time-budget and sample-efficiency ablations are retained in Appendix J.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's new performance-spectrum box plots describe variation across hyperparameter configurations rather than uncertainty from repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical results for distribution transfer and TSPLIB and replaces v1's dedicated default/tuned table with configuration-spectrum results. Retained generalization entries also change: DIMES's TSP-10000 original-scale gap changes from 3.85% in v1 Table 4 to 3.05% in v2 Table 2, while its transfer gap remains 4.29%. These are reporting revisions, not established same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The TSP objective, optimality-gap definition, MCTS equations, empirical neighbor distribution, and GT-Prior mapping retain their mathematical content. The separately numbered tour-length equation in v2 restates existing mathematics; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about MCTS tuning and simple-prior competitiveness remain. v2 extends the claimed generalization from problem scales to distribution shifts and explicitly presents standardized hyperparameter tuning as a contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking structural priors to distribution robustness and discusses distribution-dependent tuning failures on TSPLIB. Appendix L introduces explicit limits concerning Euclidean TSP, TSP-specific k-opt actions, empirical tuning, and untested alternative search mechanisms, substantially expanding v1's brief future-work discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 256 GB of memory and explicitly describes selecting configurations by average tuning-set gap. It removes v1 Section 5.1's 3000-solution and 128-solution counts for estimating the prior. The CPU, detailed configuration tables, prior arrays, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Fang et al.'s INViT work for distribution generation and Reinelt's TSPLIB, and removes the Gurobi manual reference. Its positioning emphasizes evaluation and fair comparisons while retaining the central critique of prioritizing heatmap sophistication.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial main-text passages are rewritten. v2 combines foundations and related-work discussion, introduces an evaluation-methodology section organized around three questions, and moves the original main-text ablations to Appendix J. This is extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 introduces performance-spectrum plots, a colored distribution-results table, TSPLIB tables and instance visualizations, and expanded prior-distribution plots. It also shortens the main benchmark table while retaining the full table in the appendix, compresses the main generalization table, and rearranges SHAP panels.

improvement.justification: The added distribution and TSPLIB evaluations provide useful evidence about transfer successes and failures, while Appendix L clarifies applicability limits. These improve the paper's empirical reach and interpretation. The gain is tempered by unreconciled tuning-spectrum versus benchmark values—for example, DIFUSCO's TSP-500 tuned gap is 0.09% in Section 4.2 but 0.33% in Table 1—and the removal of prior-estimation sample counts.
